questions.question: Which set of side lengths can form a valid triangle?
questions.marking_scheme_solution: 5 + 10 = 15 > 12. Sum of two smaller sides exceeds the third side. [1 Mark]

questions.question: A triangle with all three sides of unequal lengths is called a/an:
questions.marking_scheme_solution: Scalene triangle has 3 distinct side lengths (a != b != c). [1 Mark]

questions.question: Why is an equilateral triangle constructible for ANY side length s > 0?
options: A) Because s + s = 2s > s is always true for positive s
questions.correct_answer: A) Because s + s = 2s > s is always true for positive s
questions.marking_scheme_solution: Triangle inequality s + s > s holds universally for any s > 0. [1 Mark]

questions.question: If two sides of a triangle measure 6 cm and 10 cm, what is the allowable range for the third side x?

Assertion (A): Side lengths 3 cm, 3 cm, and 7 cm CANNOT form a triangle.
Reason (R): The sum of the two smaller sides (3 + 3 = 6) is less than the third side (7), violating the Triangle Inequality Theorem.
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.correct_answer: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.marking_scheme_solution: 3 + 3 = 6 < 7. Both A and R are true and R explains A. [1 Mark]

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The direct path between two points A and B is always shorter than a detour path through a third point C.
Reason (R): In triangle ABC, side AB is strictly less than the sum of sides AC + CB.
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.correct_answer: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.marking_scheme_solution: Direct path c < a + b. Both A and R are true and R explains A. [1 Mark]

questions.question: Test triangle existence for side lengths 24 cm, 26 cm, and 28 cm.
questions.marking_scheme_solution:
Smallest two sides sum = 24 + 26 = 50 cm. [1 Mark]
Longest side = 28 cm. Since 50 > 28, a triangle EXISTS. [1 Mark]

questions.question: Find the range of possible third side lengths 'x' for a triangle with sides 8 cm and 15 cm.
questions.marking_scheme_solution:
Lower limit: 15 - 8 = 7 cm. [1 Mark]
Upper limit: 15 + 8 = 23 cm.
Range: 7 cm < x < 23 cm. [1 Mark]

questions.question: Explain why compass arcs of radii 3 cm drawn from endpoints of a 7 cm base segment fail to intersect.
questions.marking_scheme_solution: Sum of radii = 3 + 3 = 6 cm. Base distance = 7 cm. Since 6 < 7, the two arcs fall short of each other and cannot meet. [2 Marks]

questions.question: Prove why an equilateral triangle exists for any positive side length s > 0.
questions.marking_scheme_solution: Sides are s, s, s. Sum of any two = s + s = 2s. Since s > 0, 2s > s is always true. Thus triangle inequality holds. [2 Marks]

questions.question:
Classify the following triangles by side lengths:
(i) 7 cm, 7 cm, 10 cm
(ii) 6 cm, 8 cm, 10 cm
questions.marking_scheme_solution:
(i) 7, 7, 10 -> Isosceles Triangle (2 sides equal). [1 Mark]
(ii) 6, 8, 10 -> Scalene Triangle (3 sides unequal). [1 Mark]

questions.question:
Test triangle existence for the following FOUR side length sets with full step-by-step reasoning:
(i) 1 cm, 1 cm, 5 cm
(ii) 2 cm, 4 cm, 8 cm
(iii) 10 cm, 20 cm, 25 cm
(iv) 1 cm, 100 cm, 100 cm
questions.marking_scheme_solution:
(i) 1 + 1 = 2 < 5 => Triangle DOES NOT exist. [1 Mark]
(ii) 2 + 4 = 6 < 8 => Triangle DOES NOT exist. [1 Mark]
(iii) 10 + 20 = 30 > 25 => Triangle EXISTS. [1 Mark]
(iv) 1 + 100 = 101 > 100 => Triangle EXISTS. [1 Mark]

questions.question:
A surveyor maps three town locations A, B, C with road distances:
- AB = 12 km
- BC = 20 km
- AC = 40 km
(i) Check if towns A, B, C can form a triangular path.
(ii) Prove whether the map claim is mathematically accurate or inaccurate.
questions.marking_scheme_solution:
(i) Sum of two shorter roads AB + BC = 12 + 20 = 32 km. [1.5 Marks]
  Longest road AC = 40 km. [1 Mark]
(ii) Since 32 km < 40 km, AB + BC < AC, violating the Triangle Inequality Theorem. [1 Mark]
  The map claim is mathematically INACCURATE; towns A, B, C lie in a non-triangular configuration. [0.5 Mark]

questions.case_scenario:
Case Study: Roof Truss Design
An architect designs a triangular roof truss with fixed bottom beam AB = 12 meters and left rafter AC = 8 meters. The right rafter BC has variable length 'x' meters.

sub_questions.sub_q: (a) Calculate the minimum allowable length for right rafter BC so that a truss triangle can be formed.
sub_questions.solution: Minimum x: x + 8 > 12 => x > 4 meters. [2 Marks]

sub_questions.sub_q: (b) Calculate the maximum allowable length for right rafter BC.
sub_questions.solution: Maximum x: x < 12 + 8 => x < 20 meters. [2 Marks]

sub_questions.sub_q: (c) State the complete allowable length range for rafter BC.
sub_questions.solution: Allowable range: 4 meters < x < 20 meters. [2 Marks]
